provenance.notes: Two packed sequences with different histories. The first sequence's two new tokens land at absolute slots 3 and 4, so the scatter crosses a block boundary and the attention reads two physical blocks.
Q, K, and V are packed into one query row while preserving the two-sequence paged schedule.
Only the updated key-cache alias is requested; the optional value-cache result is omitted.
slot_mapping names each token's flat cache slot directly; these values reproduce the derived mapping, and this case requests only the updated value-cache alias.
A negative slot suppresses that token's cache write. The cache slot retains its prior contents and remains available to attention.
Packed [Q|K|V] with an explicit slot mapping, so the scatter reads K and V out of the query row and binds no schedule tensors at all.
One decode token whose history spans two full blocks and lands at the start of the third.
num_heads equals kv_num_heads, so the grouped-query mapping is the identity.
A 71-key history exceeds one workgroup tile, and the block table is deliberately not the identity, so the online-softmax merge runs over multiple tiles rather than a single one.
A head dimension wider than the tile's per-thread share, so the accumulator loop strides.

Expected values are independently derived from the ONNX Runtime schema after rounding every tensor to its declared float16 dtype. A nonidentity block table [2, 0, 1] places the two new tokens in physical blocks 0 and 1.

A 301-key history over a 512-key block table, which is what puts the split-K schedule above its two-split floor: four contiguous key ranges of 76 keys each cross a workgroup tile boundary, so every range runs the tile loop more than once and the merge folds four non-empty online states. Grouped-query (2 query heads per KV head) so the split epilogue writes both streams.

One key of history over a 256-key block table: the split schedule is two ranges of one key each, so the second range covers nothing. It is the split that must write the (-FLT_MAX, 0) identity rather than a normalized row, and the merge must fold that identity away.
A 201-key history over a 256-key cache table with explicit slot mapping checks attention over multiple key ranges and cache publication.
The split-K schedule reading a packed [Q; K; V] query row, so the split pass strides the packed query layout while the merge writes the unpacked output.
A packed query row and explicit slot mapping exercise the split-K scatter path with both optional layout modes active.

A 32:1 multi-query decode with head size 64 stages 24,832 bytes of query, output, and probability data per workgroup. The case therefore declares a 32 KiB workgroup-storage requirement and must be rejected as inapplicable at the WebGPU 16 KiB minimum.
A large scatter workload crosses the WebGPU dispatch-grid limit. One-token sequences bound attention cost; nonzero dyadic cycles expose missing tail writes and misplaced cache/value elements.
